subject: Urgent: production p95 spike — model-12b (MeridianPay)
messages:
From: Asha Raman <asha.raman@meridianpay.com>
To: jasmine.liu@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 20 Jun 2028 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Latency increase in prod after model-12b rollout

Hi Jasmine,

We're seeing our p95 latency climb from ~220ms to ~980ms over the last 15 minutes on requests routed to model-12b. This is impacting checkout flows for ~12% of sessions (US-west). The site is still up but errors are increasing and our front-end team is starting to throttle.

I've attached a small sample of the logs and a screenshot from our APM. Can you confirm whether Redwood pushed any model variants or config changes in the last hour? We need an immediate mitigation plan — if you have a fallback available, please let us know the timeline to switch.

Thanks,
Asha Raman
Head of Platform Reliability
MeridianPay

Attachments: meridianpay_p95_logs_20280620.csv, customer-request-screenshots.png

From: jasmine.liu@redwood.ai
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Cc: seang@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 20 Jun 2028 09:40:12 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Latency increase in prod after model-12b rollout

Marissa — FYI, MeridianPay just reported a sharp p95 spike after our model-12b rollout at 08:55 PT. Asha attached sample traces. I tried a quick check in the console and the model variant profiles show slightly higher token compute time on g4x pods for this customer route.

Can you advise immediate mitigations? Two asks from Meridian: 1) they want traffic held back from model-12b (circuit-breaker) or rolled to model-11-quant if that's safe, and 2) an SLA carveout window if we need to flip.

Please propose the fastest action and any authorization needed to change routing for a single customer.

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Date: Tue, 20 Jun 2028 10:05:33 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Latency increase in prod after model-12b rollout

Jasmine — thanks for flagging and forwarding the traces. Quick triage notes:

- Confirmed: model-12b variant m12b-prod-v3 was rolled at 08:54 PT for the customer route; canary completed at ~08:58.
- Observed: increased kernel-level tail latency on a subset of g4x hosts (spike in attention kernel times). Not widespread across all customers but concentrated on MeridianPay's routing shard.
- Risk: a full rollback to m11-quant will reduce latency but may affect answer quality slightly on some prompt shapes.

Mitigation options (ranked by speed):
1) Traffic circuit-breaker (hold new sessions on older model variant) for MeridianPay only — fastest, ~5-10m to push and validate.
2) Immediate rollback of m12b to m11-quant for the MeridianPay route — ~10-20m including canary and monitoring.
3) Autoscaling burst to different instance types to absorb kernel noise — ~20-30m, higher cost and not guaranteed.

I need explicit authorization for option 1 or 2 (customer-facing change & SLA implication). If we do option 1, we should also request a temporary SLA exception window from control plane so we don't breach internal SLOs while we validate.

I'll stage the circuit-breaker config and a rollback playbook; if you can get authorization from leadership for a 60-minute carveout, we can proceed immediately.

Attachments: model12b-kernel-trace-snippets.tar.gz

--
Marissa Cole
Principal SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: seang@redwood.ai
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, jasmine.liu@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 20 Jun 2028 10:20:07 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Latency increase in prod after model-12b rollout

Marissa / Jasmine — good triage. I authorize option 1 (traffic circuit-breaker) for MeridianPay immediately and approve a 60-minute SLA carveout while we verify stability. Please follow these constraints:

- Implement circuit-breaker scoped to MeridianPay routing key only (no global routing changes).
- Start with 100% hold on new sessions to m12b for the account, verify p95 for two consecutive 5-minute windows, then reintroduce 25% test traffic if stable.
- Notify Sales/CS and MeridianPay once hold is active and provide an estimated time-to-resolve (ETR).
- Capture all logs and tag traces with rollback_authorized=true for postmortem.

Marissa, you have green light to push the config. Jasmine, loop Asha with the plan below and offer the fallback to m11-quant if the hold doesn't stabilize within 30m.

—Sean Gallagher
VP, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: jasmine.liu@redwood.ai
To: Asha Raman <asha.raman@meridianpay.com>, ops-alerts@meridianpay.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, seang@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 20 Jun 2028 10:35:02 -07:00
Subject: Re: Latency increase in prod after model-12b rollout

Asha — quick update and plan:

1) We are enabling a traffic circuit-breaker for MeridianPay only. This will hold new sessions from being routed to model-12b and keep them on m11-quant. We expect the change to take ~5–10 minutes to propagate.
2) Sean authorized a 60-minute SLA carveout while we verify stability; if p95 does not return to baseline within 30 minutes we'll roll to m11-quant fully for the MeridianPay route.
3) We'll monitor p95 in the console and share live logs. Marissa will attach kernel traces and tag the incident for the postmortem.

Apologies for the disruption; we appreciate the quick signal from your team. I'll send a follow-up once we have two consecutive stable windows or if we need to take further action.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
